grounding.states: large eggs dropped into boiling water: 12 to 13 minutes gives fully hard-boiled eggs
grounding.from: Healthline says 12 to 13 minutes gives fully hard-boiled eggs that are not over-cooked

grounding.states: large eggs in boiling water at 10 minutes: mostly cooked, slightly soft in the center
grounding.from: At 10 minutes, the eggs are mostly cooked through but slightly soft in the center

grounding.states: large eggs in boiling water past about 14 to 15 minutes: rubbery whites and dry, powdery yolks
grounding.from: 15 minutes gives rubbery whites and powdery dry yolks

grounding.states: smaller eggs cook quicker than large ones
grounding.from: smaller ones cook quicker while larger ones need extra time

grounding.states: move the eggs to cold or ice water after cooking to stop the cooking
grounding.from: Several sources move the eggs to cold or ice water after cooking to stop the cooking

value.answer: For large eggs dropped into boiling water, go about 12 minutes for a fully hard yolk. At 10 minutes they're firm but a bit soft in the middle, and past 14 or 15 minutes they get rubbery and dry. Smaller eggs cook a little quicker, so go a bit under. Then move them straight into cold water to stop them cooking.
